title: Reading Drill — Testing boat landing signs — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Testing boat landing signs — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Cairnford, work on rowers missing the direction sign during low tides had already produced a small collection of marker buoys. The harbour patrol used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: the number of missed turns.

**B** The group kept a second sign pointing upriver for the new trial, which was planned to run for nine weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that strong reflections should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
